notes.verdict: Overfit claim is right in conclusion, partly wrong in mechanism. METR's curve failed because it ran past its own 16h reliability ceiling, because frontier reward hacking makes the number swing 11.3h-to-270h on a scoring judgement (METR's own June 2026 GPT-5.6 Sol evaluation), and because coverage stopped in April 2026 — not because a lab was shown to have trained on HCAST.

notes.quote_verification_method: Every [n] source was fetched with curl (or, for two PDFs, downloaded and extracted with pdftotext -layout) and each quoted string was checked programmatically against the fetched bytes and against the same bytes with HTML tags stripped. sources.md records, per entry, which of those two matched — this matters for scripts/verify-sources.py, which greps character-by-character.
notes.lesswrong_note: Source [39] (lesswrong.com/posts/2RwDgMXo6nh42egoC) counts as verified: lesswrong.com serves a Vercel JS challenge to curl, so its quotes were verified character-by-character against the byte-identical GreaterWrong mirror, which sources.md discloses and links. A registry that fetches with curl should cite the GreaterWrong URL.
